lines.text: Long after the Republic fell, the galaxy learned to speak quietly. Fleets moved between the stars without explanation, and whole worlds simply stopped answering.
In the dark between systems, a rebellion has done something reckless. It has stolen the design of an Imperial station large enough to end a world. Now it is running.
Above the desert world of Tatooine, a stolen secret races through the dark. Inside a battered diplomatic ship, a princess carries the design of a weapon powerful enough to silence an entire planet.
The planet below keeps no record of what passes overhead. Sand, wind, and two suns. It does not yet know that its sky is about to become a battlefield.
The runner's engines are already past their limit. Behind her, something vast has held the same course for nine hours, and has never once fallen behind.
The Imperial destroyer does not hurry. It simply arrives. A wedge of grey iron more than a mile long, blotting out the stars, and then the planet.
Turbolasers find the small ship's shields. Every hit is a decision made somewhere on that bridge, and delivered without anger.
There is no answer to a ship that size. Her shields fail one section at a time, and then her engines go dark.
Held in a tractor beam, the diplomatic ship is drawn close enough for the two crews to count each other's windows. Boarding tubes lock onto the hull.
Inside, the corridor lights turn red. The people aboard have about ninety seconds.
The defenders are ship's crew, not soldiers. They take the angles they can hold, and they wait for a door that is already turning white.
The boarding party comes through the smoke in white armour, moving like one machine. A corridor this narrow leaves little room to be brave in.
When the shooting stops, something else steps through the breach. The air does not get colder. Everyone aboard feels it anyway. He does not draw a weapon. He has never needed to.
Elsewhere on the ship, the princess is doing the only useful thing left. She pulls the stolen plans out of the ship's memory before the Empire can seal it.
This is the whole design. Every corridor, every reactor line, and the one place it fails.
She gives them to a small repair droid. No rank, no clearance, no reason for anyone to search it. Then she adds a message for one old friend on the world below.
It is a thin plan. It is the only plan.
The droids reach a launch bay near the stern. One of them is certain this is a catastrophic mistake, and says so continuously. The other does not slow down.
I want it recorded that I objected. Repeatedly. And in writing.
The clamps let go. An unarmed pod drops away from a captured ship, beneath the guns of an Imperial fleet, and not one gunner spends a shot on it.
It falls toward the desert. The two ships above it shrink into the dark, and the plans that could break an empire go down into the sand.

This war will be remembered for its fleets and its heroes. It turned here. Quietly, inside a machine that cannot fight, carrying a secret it does not understand, toward a farm boy no one has thought to ask.
